title: Standard SLO + burn-rate dashboards (tier/region/model) + alert rule templates w/ runbook annotations
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Adds a standard, tier-aware SLO dashboard set (Hosted/Dedicated) and burn-rate alert rule templates with required annotations (owner, runbook, escalation channel).
body:
Overview: This PR adds a standardized dashboard and alerting pack for the Tiered SLO definitions + error budget program. It introduces (1) a consistent Grafana dashboard set for SLO status + error budget burn rate, sliceable by tier/region/model/route, and (2) templated Prometheus alert rules for multi-window burn-rate alerting with required annotations linking to runbooks and the Confluence policy. The intent is to make it trivial for services participating in the SLO program to adopt the same dashboard/alert UX and to ensure every burn alert is actionable (owner + runbook + comms guidance).

Motivation / context: We currently have a mix of ad-hoc SLO dashboards (different naming, different SLI definitions, and missing links to response guidance). As we move to enforcement (release gates + routing mitigations), we need the same indicators and burn-rate semantics across regions and tiers, otherwise oncall noise and false positives will block rollout. This PR implements the conventions agreed in ENG-2425 and aligns alerting with the burn-rate standard.

What’s included:
- Dashboards (Grafana):
  - "SLO Overview — Hosted" and "SLO Overview — Dedicated" (summary + drill-down)
  - "SLO Burn Rate — Multi-window" (quick detection vs sustained burn)
  - "SLO Latency — Streaming vs Non-streaming" (TTFT vs end-to-end where applicable)
  - "SLO Errors — 5xx/Timeouts/Disconnects" (stacked breakdown + top routes)
  - "SLO Dimensions" panel group (tier, region, model, route selectors) with guardrails on high-cardinality selectors
- Alerts (PrometheusRule templates):
  - Fast burn: 5m/1h windows (page) tuned by tier
  - Slow burn: 30m/6h windows (ticket) tuned by tier
  - Optional SLO alert variants for latency SLIs (p95/p99) where teams have stabilized the SLI definitions
- Required alert annotations:
  - owner_team, slack_channel (#eng-sre for shared, tier-specific overrides), runbook_url, dashboard_url, policy_url
  - "mitigation_hint" with a short pointer (throttle / fallback / rollback) to reduce time-to-action
- Documentation:
  - README for adopting the dashboards + rules, including a checklist for validating label dimensions (tier/region/model/route) against cardinality budgets
  - Naming conventions and folder layout for Grafana (e.g., "Reliability/SLO/{Tier}/{Region}")

Implementation notes:
- All dashboards are generated via jsonnet (consistent with existing observability-pack patterns) and share a common library:
  - dashboards/lib/slo_panels.libsonnet: common panels (availability, burn, latency, disconnects)
  - dashboards/lib/variables.libsonnet: standardized variables for tier/region/model/route with allowlists and sane defaults
- The dashboards assume the tier label is propagated as "tier" with values "hosted" | "dedicated" (aligns with redwood PR #18433). For older metrics that only include "product_tier", we include a temporary label_replace shim in the query snippets and document it as migration-only.
- Alert rules are parameterized using a small values file:
  - alerts/slo/values.yaml includes thresholds per tier and default routing (page vs ticket). Dedicated pages route to dedicated-oncall, Hosted pages route to platform-oncall (final routing change lands in redwood PR #18571; this PR provides the templates + annotations).
- Cardinality controls:
  - For dashboards, model/route breakdown panels use TopK + group-by on "model_family" by default, with an opt-in toggle to show full model for low-volume regions.
  - We avoid aggregating by both route and model in the same query for the global panels (this was one of the sources of expensive queries in the scratchpad).

Changed areas / files (high level):
- dashboards/slo/overview_hosted.jsonnet
- dashboards/slo/overview_dedicated.jsonnet
- dashboards/slo/burn_rate.jsonnet
- dashboards/slo/latency_streaming.jsonnet
- dashboards/lib/slo_panels.libsonnet
- dashboards/lib/variables.libsonnet
- alerts/slo/burn_rate_rules.yaml (template)
- alerts/slo/latency_rules.yaml (template, initially disabled)
- alerts/slo/values.yaml
- docs/slo_dashboards_and_alerts.md

Illustrative snippets (for reviewers):
- Burn rate query pattern (fast burn): rate(sli_errors_total{tier="$tier",region=~"$region"}[5m]) / rate(sli_requests_total{tier="$tier",region=~"$region"}[5m]) and compare against error_budget_burn_rate_threshold{tier="$tier",window="5m"}.
- Required annotations example: annotations: { runbook_url: "https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ONCALL/Error+budget+exhaustion+response", policy_url: "https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Error+budget+policy", dashboard_url: "https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/slo-burn-rate", slack_channel: "#eng-sre", owner_team: "sre" }.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: land dashboards + templates in observability-pack; SRE will import dashboards into the Reliability folder and validate across 2 pilot regions (us-east, eu-west) for Hosted + 1 Dedicated pilot pool.
- Phase 2: enable burn-rate rules for pilot services only (warn-only / ticket-only where needed); we’ll switch paging on once false positive rate is acceptable.
- Phase 3: expand adoption as tier-aware SLI instrumentation rolls out broadly.

Testing / validation:
- jsonnetfmt + jsonnet compilation checks (dashboards render)
- promtool check rules for YAML alert rules
- Manual spot-check: compared dashboard availability vs existing SLI scratch queries for Hosted /chat/completions streaming in us-east (within ~0.02% variance after excluding 4xx and client abort disconnects).

Review notes / discussion highlights:
- Allison Grant: Requested that every alert include a runbook link and an explicit owner, plus a short mitigation hint. Updated templates accordingly and added a lint check in docs (follow-up task to automate linting in CI).
- Aisha Bello: Asked to split streaming latency into TTFT and overall duration panels to match the SLI spec direction. Added separate panels and ensured the default view is TTFT for streaming endpoints.
- Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman: Flagged risk of high-cardinality model/route selectors. Adjusted defaults to model_family + TopK and added a warning note + suggested metric label controls (ties to ENG-2424).
- Caleb Johnson: Requested we include trace links only as optional panel links (not hard requirements) due to partial tracing coverage. Implemented as conditional links in the panel library.

CI status:
- build: pass
- lint (jsonnet): pass
- promtool rules: pass
- dashboard render snapshot: pass

Merge: Squash merged to main.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Add a lightweight CI linter to enforce presence of required alert annotations across all rules in this repo.
- Once redwood tier label propagation is fully rolled out, remove the migration label_replace shim from dashboard queries.
- Add Dedicated pool readiness panels once the readiness SLI emission is generally available (tracks ENG-2419 / redwood PR #18474).
commits: dashboards: add tier-aware SLO overview dashboards for Hosted/Dedicated
dashboards: add burn rate + latency (streaming/non-streaming) dashboards
alerts: add burn-rate PrometheusRule templates w/ tier thresholds + annotations
docs: adoption guide + naming conventions + cardinality guardrails
chore: jsonnet refactors to share SLO panel library + variables
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Dashboard looks good. Please ensure every alert rule template includes owner_team + runbook_url annotations. Also add a short mitigation hint so oncall can act faster.
Sergio Costa (author): Done. Added required annotations to both fast/slow burn templates + mitigation_hint. Also updated docs to treat these as mandatory.
Aisha Bello (review): For streaming, can we make TTFT the primary latency panel and keep end-to-end as secondary? Otherwise we’ll get a lot of noise from long outputs.
Sergio Costa (author): Updated: separate TTFT and total stream duration panels, TTFT first. Also made the dashboard default to TTFT for routes tagged streaming=true.

Nadia Rahman (review): Concern: variables allow selecting model + route simultaneously. That will encourage expensive queries. Can we default to model_family and restrict full model breakdown to TopK panels only?
Sergio Costa (author): Agreed. Default variable is model_family; full model only appears in TopK panels and has a note about cost. Removed the global panels that grouped by both route and model.
Logan Wright (review): +1. Also please add a note on label budgets and how to validate cardinality before enabling per-route/per-model alerts.
Sergio Costa (author): Added a section in docs/slo_dashboards_and_alerts.md with a preflight checklist and references ENG-2424.
Caleb Johnson (review): Trace links should be optional. Not all services have trace_id propagation end-to-end.
Sergio Costa (author): Made trace links conditional (panel link appears only when $__contains("trace_id") is true).
